title: 10/6/2026 | Elda Jazmin Villegas | LTRS | Elda Jazmin Villegas's Letter in Opposition to the 765kV Lines

documents.text:
=== PUC CMT.pdf ===
October 6, 2026

Dear Commissioners of the Public Utility Commission of Texas,

   My name is Elda Jazmin Villegas, and I am a retired Marine combat veteran and 100% VA-
rated disabled veteran living in Ellis County, just outside the City of Red Oak. My
community is home to many other veterans and military families. After serving my country, I
never imagined I would ﬁnd myself ﬁghting to protect my own home and community from
the cumulative impacts of massive industrial development and the infrastructure required
to support it.

  I am submitting this public comment regarding the proposed 765 kV transmission
expansion because my community is already experiencing ﬁrsthand the consequences of
unprecedented data center growth. Approximately 27% of the land within the City of Red
Oak has already been allocated for data center development. My own property sits directly
adjacent to more than 800 acres approved for industrial development intended for another
massive data center campus. My family didn’t move next to a data center. The data center
came to us.

   Now Texans are being asked to accept another layer of infrastructure across our
communities to accommodate extraordinary new electrical demand. I understand that
Texas needs a reliable electric grid. What I question is whether building enormous amounts
of new transmission infrastructure to accommodate unprecedented industrial loads, while
ordinary Texans bear the impacts and costs, can reasonably be characterized as protecting
the reliability of that grid.

   Before Texas commits billions of dollars and thousands of acres of private property to
this infrastructure, the Commission should fully examine what portion of the projected
need is being driven by data centers and other large-load customers, who beneﬁts from
this expansion, who pays for it, and what happens to the communities that are expected to
host both the load and the infrastructure necessary to serve it.

   In Red Oak, we’ve already watched agricultural land disappear. We’ve watched massive
industrial developments move closer to established homes. We’re facing additional
transmission infrastructure, substations, generation needs, water demands, noise, and
other impacts that don’t stop at a data center’s property line. There has to be a point at
which Texas asks not simply, “Can we build enough infrastructure to accommodate this
demand?” but “Should Texans be required to accommodate unlimited demand in the ﬁrst
place?”

  The lines drawn on transmission maps aren’t traveling through empty space. They cross
people’s land. They a]ect farms, homes, families, and communities that existed long
 before these projects were proposed. Economic development and technological
advancement shouldn’t require sacriﬁcing the Texans who already call these communities
home.

   I respectfully ask the Commission to consider the cumulative impact of large-load
development before moving forward with the proposed 765 kV transmission expansion and
to ensure that the residents bearing the consequences have a meaningful voice in these
decisions. We aren’t obstacles standing in the way of progress. We are Texans, and we
deserve to be considered part of it.



Sincerely,



Elda Jazmin Villegas
Red Oak, TX - Say NO MORE Data Centers
